name: Aethelgard: Agentic OS
tag: Assembles an agent workstation from reusable skills, subagents and tool connections.

scenarios.title: Set up a sales-ops workstation
scenarios.ask: Build a workstation for our sales-ops team of {seats} with {tools} connected tools and a {review} review policy.
steps: Skill library
Picked {=tools + 3} skills: pipeline cleanup, quote drafting, meeting notes and one per connected tool.
MCP connector
Linked {tools} tools through MCP servers with read-only access by default.
Subagent builder
Created 3 subagents: Researcher, Drafter and Checker. Each gets only the skills it needs.
Policy
Set the review rule to {review}. About {=review * 4} approvals a day per person at normal volume.
Workspace
Issued {seats} workstations from one shared template so updates reach everyone.
followups: Can people add their own skills?
Yes. A new skill is a short instruction file plus any scripts. Admins approve it once and it appears for everyone on the template.
What does read-only by default mean?
Each connection starts with read access only. Write access, such as updating a CRM record, is switched on per skill and logged.

scenarios.title: Automate a weekly report
scenarios.ask: Our team spends {hours} a week building a status report from {sources} sources. Turn it into a skill.
steps: Recorder
Watched one manual run and listed {=sources * 3 + 2} repeatable actions.
Skill writer
Wrote a report skill with one fetch step per source and a fixed layout.
Subagent
Assigned a Checker subagent that compares totals with last week and flags jumps over 20%.
Scheduler
Set the skill to run every Friday at 7 a.m. and post a draft for review.
followups: What if a source is down?
The skill marks that section as missing and still posts the rest, so the report is never silently wrong.
Can we change the layout later?
Yes. The layout is part of the skill file. Edit it once and the next run uses it.

scenarios.title: Audit agent permissions
scenarios.ask: We have {agents} agents running with {conns} tool connections. Show who can do what.
steps: Inventory
Listed {agents} agents, {conns} connections and every skill that uses them.
Permission map
Built a grid of agent by tool with read, write or none.
Risk check
Found {=max(1, round(agents * 0.15))} agents with write access they have not used in 30 days.
Fix list
Drafted a change list to drop the unused write access. Nothing changes until you approve.
followups: How often should we run this?
Monthly works for most teams. The audit can run on a schedule and only alert you when something changed.
Is there a log of agent actions?
Yes. Every tool call is logged with the agent, the skill, the input and the result, and the log can be exported.
